A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VIDEOPHY and VIDEOCON-PHYSICS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original human evaluations of nine video generators, automatic-evaluator results, difficulty analyses, and qualitative failure cases.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of three generators, leaderboard comparisons, correlation analyses, and a generator fine-tuning experiment.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction and VIDEOCON-PHYSICS training and scoring remain unchanged. Appendix P adds a limited model adaptation: fine-tuning Lumiere-T2I2V on 1,000 training pairs selected for positive semantic-adherence and physical-commonsense labels.

E1.justification: The 688 captions, three material-interaction categories, and easy/hard coverage remain unchanged. V2 additionally reports testing GPT-4-expanded longer captions in the page 5 footnote, introducing a limited new input scenario, although its extent is unspecified.

E2.justification: The generator comparison expands from nine to twelve models through actual evaluations of CogVideoX-2B, CogVideoX-5B, and Dream Machine, retaining all earlier generators. The automatic-evaluator comparator set in Table 4 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds protocols for automatic rankings using mean SA/PC scores, correlations using LAION aesthetics and RAFT motion measurements, and automatic evaluation of generator fine-tuning on 1,000 selected pairs. The original 344/344 split and human-voting protocol remain. Expansion of the held-out-model experiment is unverified: v2 says remaining models, but Table 5 still specifies three and retains its earlier results.

E4.justification: New analyses test automatic-versus-human ranking agreement, associations with visual quality and motion, and whether selected VIDEOPHY data improves a generator (Appendices M, O, and P). CogVideoX and Dream Machine failure studies are added, while earlier Pika- and VideoCrafter2-centered comparative case studies are replaced.

E5.justification: V2 introduces paired significance tests, reporting p<0.0001 for CogVideoX-5B comparisons at a stated 95% confidence criterion, and Pearson correlation estimates. It adds no repeated-run or seed reporting or numerical confidence intervals; the existing annotation-agreement reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Existing generators' main scores are retained. New joint SA/PC scores include 39.6% for CogVideoX-5B, 18.6% for CogVideoX-2B, and 13.6% for Dream Machine. Tables 10–12 add rankings, correlations, and fine-tuning outcomes, including automatically evaluated SA declining from 46 to 36.5. Some new results conflict internally: CogVideoX-5B's fluid-fluid joint score is 43.6% in Table 3 but 18.2% in Table 7.

T1.justification: The task-template and normalized Yes/No probability equations are retained, moving from Section 3.3 to Appendix F. Expanded discussion of simulation difficulty adds no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The benchmark and evaluator contributions, and the conclusion that generators fall short of physical-world simulation, remain. The abstract's headline finding changes from Pika leading at 19.7% to CogVideoX-5B leading at 39.6%, revising the empirical claim without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretations: limitations of simulation as ground truth, entanglement of perceptual metrics, proposed data/scale explanations for CogVideoX performance, motion-related failures, and possible reasons for unsuccessful fine-tuning. It acknowledges the automatic leaderboard's Pika mismatch. Appendix A's existing demographic and coverage limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds inference settings for CogVideoX and Dream Machine, discloses 14 qualified annotators and their shared clarification channel, and describes selection of the generator fine-tuning data. The front-page access link changes from the project website to a code repository. Existing VIDEOCON-PHYSICS hyperparameters and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted positioning against simulation-grounded generation and training-free multimodal evaluation, including discussion of PhysGen and VIEScore. Additional citations support newer generators, benchmark size, and binary feedback. The central positioning as a physics-focused complement to existing video-quality benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: The motivation and evaluation explanations are substantially rewritten and expanded. Baseline descriptions and evaluator equations move to appendices, the FVD/CLIP discussion moves to related work, setup subsections are consolidated, and qualitative analysis precedes a newly separate evaluator-results section.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned and moved to the first page. Caption examples move into the main text in shortened form, while the difficulty table moves to the appendix. Comparative figures are replaced, new failure illustrations and Tables 10–12 are added, and evaluator tables are reformatted. Most earlier appendix examples are retained, including renumbered Figures 24–26 as 27–29.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful checks of evaluator validity, motion/quality associations, and training-data usefulness, alongside updated model comparisons. However, new central evidence contains unresolved contradictions: CogVideoX-5B's fluid-fluid joint score differs between Tables 3 and 7, and Table 10 incorrectly includes SVD-T2I2V among closed models. These defects weaken confidence in the updated performance and ranking claims. The benefits and reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
